question: Does the controller path (--decision-mode llm) escape Pallet Town from the S0 boot state, where the JEV path never did?

conditions.mode: llm (pure controller; the fast tier is never called)
conditions.isolation: git worktree /home/kara/proj-wt-ctrlwin (branch ctrlwin @ c8cf9dc) — separate checkpoints/, cron_logs/, .ram; the live run was NOT disturbed

verdict: SUPPORTS the architecture hypothesis. From an identical boot state the controller reached Route 1 in 13 cycles; the JEV path took ~202 episodes to get there once, and only because OR_JEV was failing over. The state available to the agent is sufficient for the transition; what JEV lacks is the topology in its projection.
caveats: n=1 episode. One 30-cycle run is a signal, not a distribution.
The transition was NOT held: it reached Route 1 at c13 and was back in Pallet Town by c22, ending there.
The controller also struggles: direction-locking was warned on 14 of 30 cycles (47%).
0 escalations is by construction in llm mode (there is no fast tier to fall back from), so the escalation metric is NOT comparable across modes — cycles-to-transition is the comparable one.
The goal (Viridian City) was NOT reached by either path.
next: Repeat as a distribution (N episodes both modes, same boot state) before this is treated as settled; and MEM-PROJ now has a concrete target — give the JEV projection the topology the controller evidently infers.
